units.title: Gilliver slip last night, for the record
units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Writing it down while it's fresh. Night of day 4, fog, 23:50 approach to Gilliver, me on forward lookout. Someone standing at the very end of the slipway where the water starts. Tall, too tall for a kid. Dark coat. No light, no torch. I hailed twice on the loud-hailer. No answer, no movement. Skipper held us off. When we came alongside the slip was empty.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: I'll confirm what I saw from the wheelhouse and no more. One figure at the foot of the slip in the forward flood, standing still, at about 23:50. Two hails, no response. I held off for roughly four minutes. When the fog thinned enough to come in, nobody was on the slip or on Harbour Road. I've logged it as a trespasser and reported it to the harbourmaster. Logged it, carried on.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: I was below watching a fuel filter, so I saw nothing and won't pretend to. What I will say is these two don't spin yarns. If Kerris says somebody was standing at the end of the slip, somebody was. People do daft things in fog. I just hope whoever it was got home and isn't lying under the slip with a turned ankle.

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Thank you, skipper, report received and logged as trespass on the slipway. I walked the slip and the foreshore at first light. No one injured, nothing left behind, no prints on the weed that I could see. Please, everyone: under byelaw 14 the slip is closed to the public during ferry operations, and in fog it is simply dangerous. Thank you.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: I was at the bow with kerris and I'll be honest I saw a shape and then the fog came back over it so I couldnt swear to the coat. kerris swears to the coat. my money's on someone off a night out trying to get two bars of signal at the end of the slip, half of gilliver does it. they probably legged it when the loud hailer went off, I would

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Finn, you were looking at your feet because you'd dropped the hat. I'm not arguing with anyone about it, I'm saying what I saw, the same as I'll say it to the harbour office. At the very end, where the water starts. Tall. Dark coat. No light. Didn't move when I hailed, either time. If it was someone after signal, they had their phone in their pocket.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: glad you're both ok... sounds like a horrible fog to come in on. we had nobody on the Lisle slip all night, I stayed till the boat left. ha, anyway, I'll keep an eye out tonight, though I'll be honest I hope there's nothing to keep an eye out for. Kerris, I've put the good kettle on for when you come through

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Nobody from Gilliver goes to the foot of that slip in fog. Not because of anything. It's just steep, and the weed's like soap. My father lost a pal off it in '61. If it was a stranger they'll not know that. Hope they're dry and home.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: For the record, if it helps the log: my station had visibility at 40 to 70 m between 23:00 and 01:00 last night, air temperature 5.2 C, no wind at all. In those conditions the forward flood would light the fog itself as much as anything in it, so a figure would be very hard to judge for distance. Not doubting you, Kerris, just adding numbers.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Thank you, that's fair and useful. I'm not saying I know how far off they were to the inch. I'm saying they were standing at the end of the slip where the water starts, because the flood lit the water line right at their feet. That part I'm sure of.

units.title: creel gear adrift, holm side
units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Coastguard notice reposted: marker buoys and floating rope adrift between the approach and the Kittering Holm shore. Owners please contact the office. I have three buoys here already, a red with a white band, two orange with 'T' painted on. If they're yours, come and collect, please, as they are cluttering my doorway. Thank you.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Red with the white band is mine. I'll be by in the morning. Lost two markers off the Holm side string, rope's not cut, just chafed through on the rocks off the old station. Happens every fog. You can't see the swell working them till it's too late.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: orange with T is the treloar boat, ill tell him. lads if you've lost gear put your initials on the buoys like your granddads did, quill is not running a lost property office. well she is, but she shouldnt have to

units.title: harbour road street lights out
units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: four street lights out on harbour road between the shop and the slip. power co-op says cable fault, council contractor to come. so its pitch black from my door to the shelter in fog. ive put the shop's outside light on all night till its fixed. if you're walking down for the late boat take a torch, i've got them

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: That'll be why the slip looked so black coming in last night. Normally the street lights give you the top of the slip and the forward flood does the rest. Without them the flood just lights fog. I've asked the office if we can rig a work lamp at the shelter as a stopgap. Paperwork is ongoing, naturally.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Street lighting's council kit on a council cable, so we can't touch it, flaming annoying as it is. I had a look on my way past. The joint by the chandlery has had water in it for years. They'll dig it up, fix it, and it'll go again next fog. Not corrosion of the line. Just a bad joint in a wet hole.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 07:20 summary, day two. Air 4.9 C, dew point 4.9 C, pressure 1033 hPa, wind calm. Visibility 50 m. The fog signal ran all night and my wife has asked me to note, for the official record, that she has not slept. Overnight minimum 4.4 C on the coast, 0.8 C at a friend's station in Brackwater. Freezing fog there tonight, I'd bet on it.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Can confirm Brackwater freezing fog's arriving. 18:30 the verges were white at the jct and the temp lights had frost on the lenses, so you're sitting at a red you can't see behind a lens you can't see through. Gritter was two vans ahead of me. First time I've been glad to be behind one.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 20:00 summary. Coast 4.1 C saturated, visibility 40 m. Brackwater friend reports minus 0.6 C and rime on the fences. That's freezing fog proper. The droplets stay liquid below zero and freeze the moment they touch something. If you must drive the reservoir road tonight, assume every surface is glass.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: 06:20 cancelled. Arrived at the slip at 06:05 to find a printed notice and a man from Sound Lines saying 'sorry' in the tone of someone who has said it forty times. Took the 07:30, which called at Lisle on the way from Gilliver. Packed. The crew were talking about something on the Gilliver slip last night, but they clammed up when they saw me listening.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Ewan, if the crew are talking among themselves, I am sure it's their business, and they will tell the harbour office if it matters. They have quite enough to do getting us across without us eavesdropping. I say this as someone who also eavesdropped, and heard only the word 'slip', which in this weather could mean anything.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Fair, Mrs Hale, and point taken. Return crossing tonight 52 minutes, a personal worst. In other news the cafe has started rationing bacon rolls, one per passenger, and a man from Gilliver tried to buy two by claiming one was for his dog. He got them. The dog was not present.

units.title: What is the Holm actually for? Theories welcome, sources better.
units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: A slightly mischievous question to start the day. The clearance is approved, the trees are coming down, and nobody has said why. In the shop yesterday I heard, in order: a hotel for very rich walkers, a data centre cooled by the sea, a wind farm, a private zoo and, from a small boy, a castle. I'd love to know which of these anyone can actually support.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: None of them, yet. The only filed document is ADC/VEG/0917, clearance only, no building. A hotel, data centre or turbines would each need a full application with drawings, an environmental assessment and, for a data centre, a grid connection the Holm doesn't have. There is no such application. If one appears I'll post the reference the same morning.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: But that's the point isn't it, no application YET. Why clear the whole island first, in a month, in winter, unless you already know exactly what's going there and want it ready? Just asking questions. Do your research on who buys empty islands. It's not hoteliers. It's people who want somewhere private for when things go wrong. A private refuge for the rich.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: What would we expect to see if it were a refuge? Supplies, a water source, a jetty that works at all states of tide, some kind of power. The Holm has a landing that dries for 200 m at springs and no mains anything. If I wanted somewhere safe I would not pick an island I couldn't get to in a fog week. I'd pick a hill near a road.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: I've been looking at the company registry this afternoon and I think I have something on how the purchase was done, which may explain some of the quiet. I would rather check it twice before posting, given my record (sorry again about the bowling club). Give me until tomorrow. It's about who bought it, not why.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: My aunt thinks it'll be a house. One big house for somebody who wants to look at Gilliver without Gilliver looking back. She's usually right about people. I don't much mind what it is so long as they leave the creel ground alone.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: It's land speculation, lads. Buy cheap, clear it, sell to a developer at three times the price. That's it. That's every 'mystery' purchase in history. Nobody builds a bunker on an island you can't reach. Now can we talk about the bus timetable.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: You're thinking about it as somewhere people go to. Think about it as somewhere with nothing around it... Nothing at all, for miles. Ask why that would matter. Ask why the trees have to go. I've said what I can.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Source? And while you look for one: this is a classic. Vague hint, no detail, the reader does the scary part themselves. I produce overnight radio. I've watched one caller's 'there's something odd about that island' turn into three callers' 'everyone knows' in a single night. Nothing in that post is information. It just sounds like it.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: Thank you, all. My tally so far: one planning reference, one practical objection about tides, one speculation about speculation, and one aunt. I'm inclined to trust the aunt. Orla, I'll be ringing in later, but I promise not to mention islands.

units.title: Night ferry and the Gilliver slip?
units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Moved here from my commute thread at Mr Pell's suggestion. Harbour Chat has an account from the night crew: on the late approach to Gilliver in the fog, someone was standing at the end of the slip and didn't answer a hail. Logged as trespass. I'm not making anything of it. I'm asking whether anyone in Gilliver was down there and can save the crew some bother.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Somebody fishing. Or somebody drunk. Or somebody fishing drunk. It's Gilliver.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Probably a person, yes, though not necessarily a drunk one. In dense fog lit from a ship's floodlight, judging height and distance is close to impossible; the fog itself glows, and anything dark in it looks bigger. A person standing still, startled by a loud-hailer, might very sensibly not answer and then walk off in the dark. I'd expect the harbourmaster to put up a sign.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Thank you for moving it, and for the careful wording. Local Oddities is the right board. Please do not name any member of the ferry crew in this thread; they have given their account in their own place and are entitled to be left to do their jobs. If anyone was on the slip, the harbour office is the place to say so.

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: I asked the market traders as Mr Pell suggested. The fruit man let me look in his storeroom: three crates, one broom, no Pebble. The baker said he'd seen a grey cat on his wall two mornings ago, but it had two white socks, not one. I went home and checked the photo just in case Pebble had grown one. She hasn't.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Will keep an eye out in the van. I do Tanners lane twice a day on the way to the yard. Grey with one white sock front left, notch in the right ear, got it. if I see her I'll stop and ring you. Have a look under parked vans as well, they like the warm engine on a cold night.

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Thank you, Davey, that's so kind. I'll look under the vans on the market car park tonight with a torch. I've printed thirty more posters. I've put one in the florist's window too, between the chrysanthemums, so everyone who buys flowers this week will know Pebble's face.

units.title: Library hours cut: petition (Tollinby and Port Ammet)
units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: In case anyone missed it: from next week Tollinby and Port Ammet libraries close at 18:00, not 19:00. That last hour is the only one I can get the kids there after my shift. There's a petition (the assistant at Tollinby has a clipboard at the desk, and there's an online one). 1. Sign it. 2. Tell the council. 3. Borrow loads of books in protest.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: Signed, and I've put a copy on my shop counter. A bookseller lives on the library's goodwill, and the late hour is when the readers I care most about come in: the shift workers, the students, the people who don't want to be at home. The council's own notice says it's about heating. I'll happily lend them a jumper.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Leaving this in General as it's a civic matter. For accuracy: the change is described in the council notice as for 'the darker months', and the council has said it will review in spring. Petitions to the council should be addressed to the Communities committee clerk if they are to be formally received. Pell.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: 06:00 Brackwater jct. Red 4 min 12. Couldn't see the light, saw the glow of it in the fog like a sad sunset. A van parked up on the verge just past the jct with its engine running and no lights, been there since I went through last night apparently. Tell the middle child I lost by two seconds.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: The middle child says 'unlucky' and has taken your 20p in spirit. School bus was 25 minutes late in the fog this morning, but the driver gave them all a mint, which has caused a craze. Someone tell the gritters about the reservoir road, my neighbour went round in a full circle by the dam gates.
